shortDescription: Writes the proxysql configuration settings between layers

options.name: action
options.description: The supplied I(action) combines with the supplied I(direction) to provide the semantics of how we want to move the I(config_settings) between the I(config_layers).

options.name: config_file
options.description: Specify a config file from which I(login_user) and I(login_password) are to be read.

options.name: config_layer
options.description: RUNTIME - represents the in-memory data structures of ProxySQL used by the threads that are handling the requests. MEMORY - (sometimes also referred as main) represents the in-memory SQLite3 database. DISK - represents the on-disk SQLite3 database. CONFIG - is the classical config file. You can only LOAD FROM the config file.

options.name: config_settings
options.description: The I(config_settings) specifies which configuration we're writing.

options.name: direction
options.description: FROM - denotes we're reading values FROM the supplied I(config_layer) and writing to the next layer. TO - denotes we're reading from the previous layer and writing TO the supplied I(config_layer)."

options.name: login_host
options.description: The host used to connect to ProxySQL admin interface.

options.name: login_password
options.description: The password used to authenticate to ProxySQL admin interface.

options.name: login_port
options.description: The port used to connect to ProxySQL admin interface.

options.name: login_unix_socket
options.description: The socket used to connect to ProxySQL admin interface.

options.name: login_user
options.description: The username used to authenticate to ProxySQL admin interface.
